investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-25T00:54–01:02Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which are already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agent (kata/peer-pods) workload has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource capacity across the 2 eligible nodes. No preemption victims were available, and the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, making scheduling impossible. The eval probe's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never progressed past pod scheduling, so no VM was allocated, no remoteState was reached, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create (check-expectations.json line 256–259) received zero evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is currently scoped to the AURA observability eval.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource exhaustion: both peer-pods-capable nodes are fully allocated, leaving no capacity for a new remote-agent pod. All three sibling checks hit the same wall within the same ~7-minute window, confirming a cluster-wide capacity ceiling rather than a transient single-pod fault.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remaining nodes lack the required label or taint that qualifies them for kata/peer-pods workloads, so horizontal scaling of generic nodes would not resolve the issue without also applying the correct labels/taints and the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource.

TERTIARY — No preemption path available: the scheduler explicitly reports 'No preemption victims found,' meaning no lower-priority pods exist on the 2 eligible nodes that could be evicted to free capacity. This rules out a transient scheduling race.

investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agent (kata/peer-pods) workload has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource capacity across the 2 eligible nodes. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is currently scoped to the AURA observability eval.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-25T00:57–01:02Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available due to Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on 2 nodes and node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4. Because the remote agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or invoking the runtime, so zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector for remote agent pods. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable, blocking agent creation and all downstream eval steps. This is an infrastructure capacity/scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents pod class in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a user-facing outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector rules, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible for remote agent pods, making the cluster structurally under-provisioned for burst or concurrent eval runs.

Tertiary — concurrent or leaked remote agent pods from prior eval runs consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without being cleaned up, reducing available capacity below the threshold needed for new scheduling.

Lower confidence — a recent change to node labels, taints, or the pod's affinity spec that reduced the eligible node set or tightened resource requests, though no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.
